findings.title: Backup code plus any TOTP value skips password
findings.body: Credential login only verifies the password when totpCode is empty (the existing `user.password && !credentials.totpCode` check). The new branch then accepts a backup code whenever backupCode is non-empty and never checks the TOTP value. A caller who knows the email and one backup code can therefore sign in by also sending any non-empty totpCode (for example "000000") and omitting or faking the password. Backup codes are meant to replace the authenticator, not the password, so this is an account takeover for any CAL user who has saved a backup code.

findings.title: Backup-code consumption is a lost-update race
findings.body: A used backup code is cleared by reading the decrypted array, setting that index to null, and writing the whole blob back. Two overlapping logins (same code twice, or two different codes) both read the same snapshot and the later write overwrites the earlier one. The same code can therefore be redeemed twice, or a code that was just consumed is restored and can be used again. The update needs to be conditional (transaction/compare-and-swap on the stored ciphertext) and should remove the code, not leave a null slot.

findings.title: IdP TOTP login cannot enter a backup code
findings.body: When login is reached with the totp query param (Google/SAML users who already have 2FA), the footer is ExternalTotpFooter, which only offers Cancel, and nothing ever sets twoFactorLostAccess. The backup-code field is only rendered from the normal Lost access button, so those users cannot submit a backup code even though authorize() would accept one. Losing the authenticator locks them out of the only UI this PR adds for recovery.

findings.title: Dismissing the dialog discards the only copy of backup codes
findings.body: Backup codes are generated once in setup, returned only in that response, and shown only after TOTP enable succeeds. Dialog open state is still controlled by onOpenChange, and only the explicit Close button calls onEnable after reset. Escape, overlay click, or any parent close on the backup-code step dismisses the codes with no acknowledgement and no later retrieval or regeneration API. The user is left with 2FA on and no backup codes, which is exactly the lockout this feature is supposed to prevent.

findings.title: No test that a backup code logs in or is single-use
findings.body: The new e2e coverage only clicks download/copy/close on the setup dialog. Nothing submits a backup code at login or on disable, checks that a bad code is rejected, or checks that a used code cannot be reused. The authorize path that consumes codes (and the password-bypass case) can ship broken while these tests stay green. The enable-and-login test also never closes the new backup-code step, so it does not actually exercise the flow users hit.
